Seminar Title:

Photocatalytic applications of Ce-MOF-derived nano-heterostructure materials for selective organic transformations and renewable H2 energy generation

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Chemistry

Speaker Name:

Nutan Prabharani Gouda ( Rollno : 524cy1003)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Hall, Chemistry Department

Date and Time:

02 Sep 2026 11.00 AM

Contact:

Braja Gopal Mishra

Abstract:

The design of multifunctional catalysts that involve synergistic action between acid-base and photocatalytic active sites is a pragmatic way to develop high-efficacy materials with potential applications in selective organic transformations and the production of renewable H2 energy.&nbsp In this context, CeO2, due to its promising surface properties, mixed cationic oxidation states (Ce3+/Ce4+), oxygen vacancies, and mild surface acid-base properties, is an ideal candidate for the design of a multifunctional catalyst. These surface features of CeO2 can be exploited for specific applications in organic transformation and H2 production. Moreover, high surface area CeO2 with controlled topology can be prepared through a metal organic framework (MOF) derived route. In addition, the optoelectronic properties of CeO2 can be improved by designing nano-heterostructure materials by integration with low-band-gap semiconductors. Based on the above considerations, in this study, a series of CeO2-CuO-MgO nanocomposites was prepared by an in situ method using Ce-/Cu-MOF as a template. The structural, morphological, textural, electronic and surface acid-base characteristics of the as-synthesized pure and composite materials were investigated comprehensively. The incorporation of Cu2+ ions into the CeO2 lattice and the consequent generation of lattice strain, oxygen vacancies and mixed-valence metal-ion states (Ce3+/Ce4+ and Cu+/Cu2+) were crucial for improved optoelectronic properties and photo-reactivity. The composite materials were demonstrated to be highly effective for one-step synthesis of b-amino alcohols as well as H2 production by water spitting reaction. The detailed results obtained from these studies will be presented in the seminar.
